Test Case Title: Standard online recording, upload, processing, review, and PDF export
Components: SATE Recorder; Wi-Fi; Supabase; Edge Functions; Cloudflare; AI service; Web App; PDF service
Objective: Verify the complete production workflow for a normal session.
Preconditions: Test user is active; recorder is assigned to the user; stable Internet is available; backend services are healthy; no existing test session uses the planned test label.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute normal speech recording; stable Wi-Fi; supported browser.
Test Steps:
1. Start a new recording.
2. Speak the unique session label at the beginning and end.
3. Stop and save the recording.
4. Wait for upload and processing to complete.
5. Open the session in the Web App.
6. Review transcript and annotations.
7. Export the SATE report as PDF.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Recorder shows clear Recording, Saved, Uploading, Processing, and Completed states. The Web App shows the correct session, audio, transcript, annotations, and report controls. PDF opens successfully.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Exactly one session record and one valid audio object are created. Status transitions are valid and terminal state is Completed. AI result is attached to the same session. No duplicate processing job is created.
Data Integrity / Validation: Confirm session ID, user ID, device ID, timestamps, duration, audio beginning/end markers, transcript-session match, valid annotation JSON, and PDF-session match.
Pass Criteria: All steps complete without manual recovery; no data loss, duplication, mis-association, or unhandled error occurs.

Test Case Title: Very short recording near the minimum supported duration
Components: SATE Recorder; Supabase; AI service; Web App
Objective: Verify expected handling of a valid recording near the minimum duration.
Preconditions: Minimum supported duration is documented or a provisional threshold is agreed for testing.
Test Data / Environment: 10-15 second recording containing one clearly spoken sentence.
Test Steps:
1. Start recording.
2. Record for the minimum supported duration.
3. Stop and sync.
4. Open the result in the Web App.
5. Attempt PDF export if the session completes.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder either accepts the session or shows a documented minimum-duration message. The Web App does not display an unexplained blank result.
Expected Backend / Data Result: If accepted, one complete session is processed. If rejected, no orphan audio, session, or processing job remains.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check actual duration, session status, transcript presence, and absence of orphan records.
Pass Criteria: Behavior matches the documented minimum-duration requirement and leaves the system in a consistent state.

Test Case Title: Silent or near-silent recording
Components: SATE Recorder; AI service; Web App
Objective: Verify that absence of speech is distinguished from pipeline failure.
Preconditions: Backend services are healthy.
Test Data / Environment: 2-minute recording with room tone and no intentional speech.
Test Steps:
1. Record two minutes of silence or near-silence.
2. Stop and sync.
3. Wait for processing.
4. Open the session in the Web App.
5. Review status, transcript, and annotations.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The session displays a clear outcome such as No Detectable Speech, Low Confidence, or an empty transcript with explanation. It must not remain indefinitely in Processing.
Expected Backend / Data Result: AI response is stored as a valid result or a defined non-speech outcome. Processing status reaches a defined terminal state.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify audio is playable and complete; transcript is not copied from another session; result JSON is valid.
Pass Criteria: The system distinguishes valid silent audio from upload/processing failure and provides an actionable status.

Test Case Title: Noisy recording with multiple speakers and interruptions
Components: SATE Recorder; AI service; Web App
Objective: Verify that difficult audio degrades recognition quality gracefully without breaking the pipeline.
Preconditions: Normal end-to-end environment is available.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute recording with background noise, two speakers, pauses, overlapping speech, and brief interruptions.
Test Steps:
1. Record the prepared noisy scenario.
2. Stop and sync.
3. Review transcript, speaker-related output if supported, annotations, warnings, and PDF.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The session completes or shows a defined low-quality warning. The UI remains responsive and does not mislabel the result as an upload failure.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One valid audio object and one result set are stored. Partial/low-confidence fields follow the documented schema.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check that output belongs to this audio, JSON fields are parseable, and no unrelated transcript appears.
Pass Criteria: The session reaches a defined terminal state with no crash, malformed data, or cross-session contamination.

Test Case Title: Session metadata, timestamp, time-zone, and device association
Components: SATE Recorder; Supabase; Web App; PDF service
Objective: Verify that metadata remains correct across recorder, backend, Web App, and exported report.
Preconditions: Recorder and phone clocks are set correctly; test account and device assignment are known.
Test Data / Environment: One 2-minute session created near a known clock time; record local time zone.
Test Steps:
1. Note user, recorder ID, local start time, and end time.
2. Record and sync a session.
3. Compare metadata in device UI, database, Web App, and PDF.
4. Refresh and reopen the session.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: User name/ID, device, date, time, duration, and session label are consistent and displayed in the intended time zone.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Canonical timestamps are stored consistently; display conversion is correct; device association does not change after refresh.
Data Integrity / Validation: Compare session ID, user ID, device ID, start/end timestamps, time zone, and calculated duration across all components.
Pass Criteria: No incorrect user/device association, unexplained time shift, or material duration discrepancy is present.

Test Case Title: Repeated Stop, Save, Upload, or Submit actions
Components: SATE Recorder; Mobile App; Supabase; Edge Functions
Objective: Verify that rapid repeated user actions do not create duplicate sessions or jobs.
Preconditions: Normal recording is in progress; tester can tap controls rapidly.
Test Data / Environment: 2-minute recording; stable network.
Test Steps:
1. End the recording.
2. Rapidly tap Stop/Save several times.
3. If an Upload or Retry control appears, tap it repeatedly.
4. Wait for completion.
5. Inspect session list and backend records.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Controls become disabled or requests are safely deduplicated. The user sees only one session.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Exactly one canonical session, one final audio object, and one final result set exist. Duplicate requests use the same idempotency key or are rejected safely.
Data Integrity / Validation: Count session records, storage objects, processing attempts, transcripts, and reports linked to the source recording.
Pass Criteria: Repeated actions never create duplicate user-visible sessions, duplicate reports, or conflicting final states.

Test Case Title: Graceful recorder restart during an active recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Supabase
Objective: Verify that a normal restart during recording does not silently lose captured audio.
Preconditions: Recorder battery and storage are sufficient; a session is actively recording.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute intended recording; restart after approximately 2 minutes.
Test Steps:
1. Start recording and speak a beginning marker.
2. After two minutes, perform a normal device restart.
3. Restart the recorder.
4. Inspect recovered/pending sessions.
5. Sync any recovered partial session.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder clearly identifies the interrupted session. Recommended behavior: preserve the recorded portion and label it Interrupted; do not silently discard it.
Expected Backend / Data Result: At most one interrupted session is created for the captured audio. Any upload uses the original session identity or a clearly linked recovery identity.
Data Integrity / Validation: Play the recovered audio; verify beginning marker, duration, file readability, status, and absence of duplication.
Pass Criteria: Captured audio is preserved or intentionally rejected according to a documented rule, and the user receives an explicit status.

Test Case Title: Forced power loss during an active recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage
Objective: Verify crash-safe local audio persistence when shutdown cannot complete cleanly.
Preconditions: Recorder is actively recording; tester can disconnect power or force shutdown safely.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute intended recording; forced shutdown after approximately 2 minutes.
Test Steps:
1. Start recording and speak a beginning marker.
2. Force power loss without using the normal stop control.
3. Restore power.
4. Inspect recovered data and device messages.
5. Sync any recoverable session.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder reports an interrupted or recovered session rather than showing a completed recording. It must not claim success if the audio is corrupted.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Recovered audio is either stored as one valid partial session or quarantined as corrupted with a traceable error. No phantom Completed session is created.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify file readability, duration, beginning marker, session count, error logs, and local cleanup behavior.
Pass Criteria: No silent data loss, false Completed state, or duplicate session occurs.

Test Case Title: Low-battery shutdown during recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Battery Management; Local Storage
Objective: Verify low-battery warnings and safe session preservation.
Preconditions: Recorder battery can be reduced to the low-battery threshold.
Test Data / Environment: Recording continues until low-battery warning and shutdown.
Test Steps:
1. Begin a recording with low remaining battery.
2. Continue until warning appears.
3. Observe whether recording stops automatically or the device shuts down.
4. Recharge and restart.
5. Inspect and sync the session.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: A warning appears early enough for action. Recommended behavior: safely stop and save before shutdown when possible.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One valid partial or completed session is preserved with an accurate reason/status. No corrupted Completed session is created.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check duration, file readability, battery-related event log, status, and upload result.
Pass Criteria: Audio captured before shutdown is handled according to the documented low-battery rule with no false success.

Test Case Title: Insufficient local storage before recording starts
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage
Objective: Verify that the recorder prevents a session that cannot be stored safely.
Preconditions: Local storage is below the defined minimum free-space threshold.
Test Data / Environment: Recorder with intentionally reduced free storage.
Test Steps:
1. Attempt to start a recording.
2. Observe the message and controls.
3. Free sufficient storage.
4. Retry recording.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder blocks recording or clearly warns the user before capture begins. After space is freed, normal recording is available.
Expected Backend / Data Result: No incomplete session or empty backend record is created from the blocked attempt.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify free-space check, absence of zero-byte files, absence of orphan session records, and successful retry after cleanup.
Pass Criteria: The user cannot unknowingly begin a recording that the device cannot preserve.

Test Case Title: Local storage becomes full during recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage
Objective: Verify safe termination when storage is exhausted during capture.
Preconditions: Recorder starts with enough space for a short recording but not for the planned duration.
Test Data / Environment: Continue recording until storage is exhausted.
Test Steps:
1. Start recording.
2. Continue until the storage-full condition occurs.
3. Observe device behavior.
4. Restart if required.
5. Inspect and sync recoverable audio.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder stops safely and shows a specific storage error. It must not continue displaying Recording after writes have failed.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Captured audio is finalized if possible, or marked corrupted/interrupted. No zero-byte Completed session is created.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check final playable duration, file size, error status, session count, and cleanup of temporary files.
Pass Criteria: The condition is detected, communicated, and handled without silent corruption or false completion.

Test Case Title: Restart during the local save/finalization step
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify crash safety while the recorder finalizes audio and creates the upload queue item.
Preconditions: A recording is ready to stop; tester can restart immediately after Stop.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute recording.
Test Steps:
1. Record five minutes.
2. Press Stop.
3. Restart the recorder while Save/Finalizing is displayed.
4. Restart and inspect session/queue state.
5. Allow synchronization.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: After restart, the session is either safely recovered and queued once or clearly marked failed. The UI must not show two copies.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Only one final audio object/session is created. Temporary files are reconciled or removed.
Data Integrity / Validation: Compare local files, queue entries, backend records, audio duration, and processing jobs.
Pass Criteria: No duplicate session, orphan temporary file affecting storage, or silent loss occurs.

Test Case Title: Restart after recording stops but before upload begins
Components: SATE Recorder; Upload Queue; Supabase
Objective: Verify persistence of a locally saved, not-yet-uploaded session.
Preconditions: Recording has stopped and is locally saved; network upload has not begun.
Test Data / Environment: 3-minute recording.
Test Steps:
1. Record and stop the session.
2. Restart immediately before upload starts.
3. Reconnect to network.
4. Observe queue recovery and final result.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The pending session reappears after restart and uploads automatically or through the documented resume action.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One queue item maps to one session. Status progresses from pending to completed without creating a second session.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify local-to-server session identity, queue persistence, audio completeness, and final status.
Pass Criteria: The pending session survives restart and completes without user re-recording.

Test Case Title: Recording starts and ends while fully offline
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Upload Queue; Supabase
Objective: Verify offline recording and automatic upload when connectivity returns.
Preconditions: Wi-Fi is disabled or unavailable before the session starts.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute recording; restore Internet after the session is saved.
Test Steps:
1. Disable connectivity.
2. Record and stop a session.
3. Confirm local Pending Upload status.
4. Restore Internet.
5. Wait without manually creating a second session.
6. Review the session on the Web App.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Recording works offline. The session is visibly queued. When Internet returns, upload starts automatically or at the documented trigger.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One queued session uploads once, processes, and reaches Completed.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify local persistence, same session ID before/after upload, complete audio, queue removal only after server acknowledgement, and no duplicate.
Pass Criteria: Offline recording is preserved and completes automatically after connectivity returns.

Test Case Title: Internet connection is lost during recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Network Detection
Objective: Verify that recording is independent of Internet availability.
Preconditions: Recording begins online.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute session; disable Internet after 1 minute and restore after Stop.
Test Steps:
1. Start online recording.
2. Disable Internet during capture.
3. Continue recording.
4. Stop the session while offline.
5. Restore Internet and wait for completion.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Recording continues without interruption. The device shows offline/pending status after Stop and later uploads normally.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One complete audio object and one session are created after reconnection.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check audio for gaps at the disconnect point, duration, queue state, and final transcript match.
Pass Criteria: No capture gap, crash, duplicate session, or misleading completion status occurs.

Test Case Title: Internet is lost after Stop but before upload starts
Components: SATE Recorder; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify correct queuing when a saved session cannot begin uploading.
Preconditions: Recording is complete; upload has not yet started.
Test Data / Environment: 3-minute recording.
Test Steps:
1. Stop the recording.
2. Immediately disable Internet.
3. Confirm Pending Upload status.
4. Restore Internet.
5. Observe automatic upload and processing.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The session remains visible and queued. No repeated user action is required unless explicitly designed.
Expected Backend / Data Result: The same session is uploaded once after reconnection. Queue state is cleared only after successful acknowledgement.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify one session, one audio object, correct status transitions, and no loss of local file before acknowledgement.
Pass Criteria: The saved session survives the outage and completes once connectivity returns.

Test Case Title: Internet drops during an active upload
Components: SATE Recorder or Mobile App; Supabase Storage; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify upload retry or resume without duplication or file corruption.
Preconditions: An upload large enough to interrupt is in progress.
Test Data / Environment: 10-minute or larger session; disable Internet at approximately 40% upload.
Test Steps:
1. Start upload.
2. Disable Internet mid-transfer.
3. Wait for failure detection.
4. Restore Internet.
5. Allow automatic retry/resume.
6. Inspect backend and Web App.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The session changes to a retryable/pending state and later completes. The UI does not remain permanently stuck at Uploading.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Upload resumes or restarts according to the documented strategy. Incomplete objects are overwritten, completed, or cleaned safely. One final session exists.
Data Integrity / Validation: Compare local/server file size, duration, checksum if available, beginning/end markers, object count, and processing job count.
Pass Criteria: The final server audio is complete and playable, with exactly one user-visible session and no orphan file that affects later processing.

Test Case Title: Connectivity returns while app/device is in background or screen is locked
Components: SATE Mobile App; SATE Recorder; OS Background Services; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify the documented background upload behavior.
Preconditions: A session is pending offline; mobile app is backgrounded or phone is locked before Internet returns.
Test Data / Environment: Pending 5-minute session; supported phone OS.
Test Steps:
1. Create an offline pending session.
2. Background the app or lock the phone.
3. Restore Internet.
4. Wait for the documented background window.
5. Unlock/open the app if necessary.
6. Check completion.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Upload either starts in the background as designed or begins immediately when the app is reopened. The pending session is not lost.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Queue state remains durable and the session uploads once.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify OS logs if available, queue persistence, session count, and final audio completeness.
Pass Criteria: Behavior matches the supported background policy and no session remains permanently stranded.

Test Case Title: Wi-Fi is connected but Internet access is unavailable
Components: SATE Recorder; Mobile App; Network Detection
Objective: Verify that the system checks real Internet/backend reachability rather than Wi-Fi association only.
Preconditions: Connect to a router with no Internet access.
Test Data / Environment: 3-minute session.
Test Steps:
1. Connect to Wi-Fi without Internet.
2. Record and stop a session.
3. Observe upload status.
4. Restore Internet without changing Wi-Fi if possible.
5. Wait for upload.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The UI indicates Offline, Cannot Reach Service, or Pending Upload rather than claiming successful upload.
Expected Backend / Data Result: No false server acknowledgement is stored. The queue retries safely after reachability returns.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify local file remains, backend has no incomplete Completed record, and final upload creates one session.
Pass Criteria: The system does not confuse Wi-Fi connection with successful synchronization.

Test Case Title: Captive portal or authentication-required Wi-Fi
Components: SATE Recorder; Mobile App; Network Detection
Objective: Verify safe behavior on a network that requires browser sign-in.
Preconditions: Connect to a captive-portal network without completing sign-in.
Test Data / Environment: 3-minute pending session.
Test Steps:
1. Connect to captive-portal Wi-Fi.
2. Attempt sync.
3. Complete portal sign-in.
4. Observe retry and completion.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The system shows a network error/pending state until Internet is usable, then retries without creating a second session.
Expected Backend / Data Result: No invalid Completed state or duplicate upload occurs.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify queue durability, one final session, and correct error recovery.
Pass Criteria: The session remains safe until the network becomes usable and then completes normally.

Test Case Title: Switch from one Wi-Fi network to another or to a hotspot during upload
Components: SATE Recorder or Mobile App; Upload Queue; Supabase
Objective: Verify transfer recovery after IP/network changes.
Preconditions: Upload is in progress and a second valid network is available.
Test Data / Environment: 10-minute recording.
Test Steps:
1. Start upload on Network A.
2. Disconnect from Network A mid-upload.
3. Connect to Network B or hotspot.
4. Wait for retry/resume.
5. Inspect final session.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The upload recovers without requiring a new recording. Status updates remain understandable.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One final audio object is committed. Any partial upload from Network A is reconciled.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check object/session counts, file completeness, processing job count, and final transcript.
Pass Criteria: Network switching does not produce corruption, duplication, or permanent Uploading state.

Test Case Title: Rapidly flapping or weak network
Components: SATE Recorder or Mobile App; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify bounded retry behavior under unstable connectivity.
Preconditions: Network can be toggled or throttled.
Test Data / Environment: 10-minute session; alternate online/offline several times.
Test Steps:
1. Start upload.
2. Alternate online and offline states several times.
3. End with a stable connection.
4. Wait for completion.
5. Review retry count and final records.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The UI does not spam duplicate sessions or become unresponsive. It eventually completes or reaches a clear retryable state.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Retries are bounded and idempotent. One canonical session and one valid final audio object remain.
Data Integrity / Validation: Review attempt count, backoff timing, session/object counts, final file integrity, and queue cleanup.
Pass Criteria: The system recovers when stability returns and never creates conflicting final states.

Test Case Title: User taps manual Retry while automatic retry is already running
Components: SATE Mobile App or Recorder; Upload Queue; Supabase
Objective: Verify that manual and automatic retry paths cannot duplicate the upload.
Preconditions: A retryable upload failure is present and automatic retry is scheduled or active.
Test Data / Environment: 5-minute failed/pending session.
Test Steps:
1. Trigger an upload failure.
2. Restore connectivity.
3. Tap Retry repeatedly while automatic retry begins.
4. Wait for final completion.
5. Inspect backend attempts and records.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Only one active upload is presented to the user. Extra taps are disabled, ignored, or safely deduplicated.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Multiple requests, if sent, resolve to one canonical session/object and one final processing result.
Data Integrity / Validation: Count upload requests, storage objects, sessions, processing jobs, and user-visible entries.
Pass Criteria: Manual/automatic retry concurrency never creates a duplicate or corrupt final session.

Test Case Title: Five recordings made consecutively while online
Components: SATE Recorder; Upload Queue; Supabase; AI service
Objective: Verify unique session creation and correct ordering for normal back-to-back use.
Preconditions: Stable network; no pending sessions.
Test Data / Environment: Recordings of 30 sec, 1 min, 2 min, 3 min, and 5 min, each with a unique spoken label.
Test Steps:
1. Create five recordings with less than 20 seconds between sessions.
2. Allow uploads to occur.
3. Review the queue and Web App.
4. Open each transcript.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: All five sessions appear once with correct order, labels, dates, and durations. Starting the next session does not overwrite the previous one.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Five unique session IDs, five correct audio objects, and five result sets are created.
Data Integrity / Validation: Match each audio beginning/end marker to its transcript; compare timestamps, duration, and session IDs.
Pass Criteria: All five sessions complete without overwrite, merging, omission, or cross-session transcript assignment.

Test Case Title: Start a new recording while the previous session is uploading
Components: SATE Recorder; Upload Queue; Local Storage; Supabase
Objective: Verify simultaneous recording and background upload, or correct prevention if unsupported.
Preconditions: Session A is uploading; recorder is ready for another action.
Test Data / Environment: Session A: 10 minutes; Session B: 2 minutes.
Test Steps:
1. Start uploading Session A.
2. Attempt to start Session B.
3. Complete Session B.
4. Wait for both sessions to finish.
5. Review results.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The UI follows the documented rule: either allows Session B safely or clearly blocks it. If allowed, statuses remain distinct.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Sessions A and B retain unique IDs, files, statuses, and processing jobs.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify no audio mixing, file overwrite, shared session ID, or status crossover.
Pass Criteria: Both sessions are handled correctly according to the documented concurrency requirement.

Test Case Title: Five offline recordings queued and uploaded later
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Upload Queue; Supabase
Objective: Verify durable multi-session queueing.
Preconditions: Device is offline and has sufficient storage.
Test Data / Environment: Five recordings with unique labels and varying lengths.
Test Steps:
1. Disable Internet.
2. Record five sessions.
3. Restart the recorder/app once while still offline.
4. Confirm all five remain queued.
5. Restore Internet.
6. Wait for all sessions to complete.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: All five queued sessions remain visible after restart and later upload. Progress/status is shown per session.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Five unique sessions and five complete audio objects are committed. Queue entries are removed only after acknowledgement.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check queue persistence, upload order, session count, audio/transcript mapping, and no duplicates.
Pass Criteria: No queued session is lost, merged, duplicated, or indefinitely blocked.

Test Case Title: One queued session fails while later sessions continue
Components: Upload Queue; Supabase; AI service
Objective: Verify that a single bad item does not block the entire queue.
Preconditions: At least three sessions are queued; a fault can be injected for Session 2.
Test Data / Environment: Three queued sessions; cause Session 2 upload or processing to fail.
Test Steps:
1. Queue Sessions 1-3.
2. Inject a failure for Session 2.
3. Restore normal service.
4. Observe Sessions 1 and 3.
5. Retry Session 2.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Each session shows its own status. Failure of Session 2 does not hide or freeze Sessions 1 and 3.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Sessions 1 and 3 reach Completed. Session 2 reaches a defined failed/retryable state and can later complete without duplication.
Data Integrity / Validation: Verify per-session attempt counts, queue progression, final session count, and audio mapping.
Pass Criteria: Queue processing is fault-isolated and recoverable.

Test Case Title: Queue order and status persist across app/recorder restart
Components: SATE Recorder or Mobile App; Upload Queue
Objective: Verify durable queue state and deterministic resumption.
Preconditions: Several sessions are Pending, Uploading, and Failed/Retryable.
Test Data / Environment: Three or more sessions in different queue states.
Test Steps:
1. Create mixed queue states.
2. Restart the recorder/app.
3. Inspect order and statuses.
4. Restore connectivity/service.
5. Observe resumption.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: All queue entries reappear with correct identities and understandable statuses.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Queue metadata is restored. No entry is silently dropped or duplicated; final states are consistent.
Data Integrity / Validation: Compare queue entries before/after restart, session IDs, attempt counts, and final records.
Pass Criteria: Restart does not alter session identity, lose queue entries, or create duplicate uploads.

Test Case Title: Same recording reaches backend through direct Wi-Fi and mobile-app paths
Components: SATE Recorder; SATE Mobile App; Supabase; Edge Functions
Objective: Verify deduplication when both supported data paths attempt to sync the same source recording.
Preconditions: Direct Wi-Fi and BLE/mobile paths are both enabled for the same test recording, or the condition can be simulated.
Test Data / Environment: One uniquely labeled 5-minute recording.
Test Steps:
1. Create one recording.
2. Trigger/allow both direct Wi-Fi and mobile-app sync paths.
3. Wait for all requests to finish.
4. Inspect backend and Web App.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The user sees one session only. Any duplicate-path message is clear and non-blocking.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Backend identifies the same source recording and commits one canonical session/audio/result. Duplicate transport attempts are linked or rejected safely.
Data Integrity / Validation: Compare source recording ID, idempotency key, session/object/job counts, and final transcript.
Pass Criteria: Dual-path delivery never creates duplicate sessions, conflicting metadata, or double processing.

Test Case Title: Recording at the 30-minute boundary
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Upload; AI service; Web App
Objective: Verify behavior at the stated long-session threshold.
Preconditions: Device is fully charged with sufficient storage and stable network.
Test Data / Environment: Exactly 30-minute session with beginning, midpoint, and end markers.
Test Steps:
1. Record exactly 30 minutes.
2. Stop and sync.
3. Wait for processing.
4. Review audio, transcript, annotations, and PDF.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: No timeout, crash, or unexplained warning occurs at the boundary. Progress remains responsive.
Expected Backend / Data Result: One complete audio object and result set are created within the documented SLA.
Data Integrity / Validation: Check complete duration, all spoken markers, file size, memory/error logs, transcript coverage, and PDF pagination.
Pass Criteria: The complete 30-minute session is preserved, processed, reviewed, and exported successfully.

Test Case Title: Forty-five-minute recording
Components: SATE Recorder; Supabase; AI service; Web App
Objective: Verify a realistic extended clinical session.
Preconditions: Battery, storage, and network are sufficient.
Test Data / Environment: 45-minute recording with markers every 10 minutes.
Test Steps:
1. Record 45 minutes.
2. Stop and sync.
3. Monitor upload and processing time.
4. Review all markers in audio/transcript.
5. Export PDF.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: Device/app remains responsive. The Web App can load and navigate the long transcript.
Expected Backend / Data Result: Audio upload and processing complete without chunk loss, duplicate jobs, or timeout beyond the documented policy.
Data Integrity / Validation: Validate duration, all interval markers, file integrity, transcript continuity, processing time, and PDF pagination.
Pass Criteria: All content is complete and usable with no resource-related failure.

Test Case Title: Maximum supported recording duration
Components: SATE Recorder; Local Storage; Backend
Objective: Verify the documented maximum duration and user warning behavior.
Preconditions: Maximum duration is confirmed by product/engineering.
Test Data / Environment: Session at the maximum duration and, if safe, an attempt to exceed it.
Test Steps:
1. Record until the maximum duration.
2. Observe warning or automatic stop behavior.
3. Attempt to continue if allowed.
4. Sync and review.
Expected Device / App / Web Result: The recorder warns before the limit and safely stops or blocks additional recording according to requirement.

Test Case Title: Save failure and concurrent transcript editing
